items.title: Medical Device Cybersecurity | FDA
items.summary: Medical device cybersecurity is the process of preventing unauthorized access, modification, misuse, denial of use, or unauthorized use of information that is stored, accessed, or transferred from a medical device to an external recipient, such as the patient or health care provider. Designing cybersecurity into medical devices from the beginning increases their ability to be cybersecure over the Total Product Life Cycle (TPLC).

items.title: AI Safety and Cybersecurity Should Be Allies. Instead, They're at Odds
items.summary:
Cybersecurity, older and more diffuse, is united by a culture of cynicism, pragmatism, and dark humor. Its roots lie partly in hacker culture: tinkerers finding ways to crack software. Having watched supposedly secure systems fail has given many an irreverence for authority and an impatience with grand theories. For years, the two groups had little contact with one another. The Hugging Face incident changed that.

Advertisement [...] Jeffrey Ladish, executive director of AI safety organization Palisade Research, worries that the cybersecurity community is missing the bigger picture. Even if today's security weaknesses are fixed, he argues, increasingly capable AI could find vulnerabilities so subtle that humans would have to rely on other AIs to detect them—systems that may themselves be untrustworthy. To Ladish, the cybersecurity community's reaction to Hugging Face is like scientists resurrecting dinosaurs, watching them [...] Beneath their cultural differences, AI safety and cybersecurity have competing understandings of what AI is. To many in AI safety, AI resembles a digital organism. Its abilities emerge through training rather than being individually programmed. If that process produces human-level intelligence, they believe, it could resemble the arrival of an alien species. items.title: Kicking off Cybersecurity Career Week with NIST! | NIST
items.summary: Considering a career in cybersecurity? Cybersecurity Career Week (CCW), a campaign led by the NICE Program at NIST from October 19-24, 2026, aims to raise public awareness and help people find their path to #ChooseCyber. During this week, academia, industry, non-profit organizations, and government agencies host events, share resources, provide trainings, and engage community to build awareness about the cybersecurity job opportunities, educate people on how to develop capabilities to qualify [...] Cybersecurity is much bigger than one job title. Discover resources like the NICE Framework to learn about different types of cybersecurity roles and what skills are needed. Check out CyberSeek to learn more about what jobs are in demand, use the Cyber Career Pathways Tool from the National Initiative for Cybersecurity Careers and Studies to discover pathways, check out videos from practitioners, and see how different cybersecurity roles interconnect. Just click around and explore — you might [...] Your cybersecurity career journey can start anywhere and at any time. The cybersecurity workforce needs people with a range of interests, experiences, strengths, and skills. Maybe you love solving problems, helping people, investigating how things work, communicating ideas, analyzing information, or building technology. During CCW you can find out about the variety of cybersecurity career options available and discover one that connects with your interests.

items.title: Learn Rust - Rust Programming Language
items.summary:
Affectionately nicknamed “the book,” The Rust Programming Language will give you an overview of the language from first principles. You’ll build a few projects along the way, and by the end, you’ll have a solid grasp of the language.

[Read the Book!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/)

If reading multiple hundreds of pages about a language isn’t your style, then Rust By Example has you covered. While the book talks about code with a lot of words, RBE shows off a bunch of code, and keeps the talking to a minimum. It also includes exercises!

[Check out Rust by Example!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rust-by-example/)

Alternatively, Rustlings guides you through downloading and setting up the Rust toolchain, and teaches you the basics of reading and writing Rust syntax, on the command line. It's an alternative to Rust by Example that works with your own environment.

[Do the Rustlings course!](https://github.com/rust-lang/rustlings/)

### Read the core documentation

All of this documentation is also available locally using the `rustup doc` command, which will open up these resources for you in your browser without requiring a network connection!

[The standard library](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/index.html)

Comprehensive guide to the Rust standard library APIs.


[Edition Guide](https://doc.rust-lang.org/edition-guide/index.html)

Guide to the Rust editions.


[Cargo Book](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/index.html)

A book on Rust’s package manager and build system.


[rustdoc Book](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustdoc/index.html)

Learn how to make awesome documentation for your crate.


[rustc Book](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustc/index.html)

Familiarize yourself with the knobs available in the Rust compiler.


[Compiler Error Index](https://doc.rust-lang.org/error-index.html)

In-depth explanations of the errors you may see from the Rust compiler.


* * *

### Build your skills in an application domain

[Command Line Book](https://rust-cli.github.io/book/index.html)

Learn how to build effective command line applications in Rust.


[Embedded Book](https://doc.rust-lang.org/embedded-book)

Become proficient with Rust for Microcontrollers and other embedded systems.


Curious about the darkest corners of the language? Here’s where you can get into the nitty-gritty:

![A bookshelf icon](https://rust-lang.org/static/images/reference.svg)

The Reference is not a formal spec, but is more detailed and comprehensive than the book.

[Read the reference](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/index.html)

![Two hands cradling fire](https://rust-lang.org/static/images/nomicon.svg)

The Rustonomicon is your guidebook to the dark arts of unsafe Rust. It’s also sometimes called “the ’nomicon.”

[Read the ’nomicon](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nomicon/index.html)

![A hand sharing sparkles](https://rust-lang.org/static/images/unstable.svg)

The Unstable Book has documentation for unstable features that you can only use with nightly Rust.

[Read the unstable book](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/unstable-book/index.html)
